title: Gateside By TSA PreCheck Brings Back A Piece Of Airport Goodbyes At Billings Logan - Mix 97.1
content: Not to sound like grandad telling you a tale about the "good old days," but way back in the pre-2001 times, going to the airport was a much different experience. Pre-9/11, there was no such thing as the TSA. Anyone, with or without a ticket, could basically walk right up to the gates. If your loved one was jetting off for work, vacation, or whatever, you could hang out at the gate as long as you'd like. Read More: Chain Stores and Restaurants Closing Locations in 2026 Perhaps you'd sit in the concourse and watch their plane take off, lingering long after the "final call for boarding" went over the loudspeakers. On the flip side, you could be right there waiting for them at the gate when they came home, instead of crowding around the baggage claim. Of course, the world will never return to what is what like before September 11, 2001, but things are getting just a tad friendlier at airports across the United States, including Billings Logan International. The TSA is rolling out the Gateside PreCheck service. According to a 10/6 press release from BIL, the program will allow qualified individuals without boarding passes to be screened and go beyond the TSA passenger screening checkpoint. “The Gateside by TSA PreCheck program is a welcome addition to the airport experience at BIL,” said Jeff Roach, Director of Aviation and Transit, “you can now go to the gate to see travelers off, greet arriving passengers, or just to experience post-security amenities at the airport.” The program only allows 50 people per day beyond the TSA security gates at BIL. You can participate anytime the TSA gates are staffed, and you must leave the concourse before 8 PM. Individuals will need to pre-register with TSA at least 24 hours in advance, but not more than three days ahead. You can do that HERE. I like this program a lot. The days of sitting by yourself for two hours before your flight can now be a thing of the past.

title: Elon Musk’s Terafab Discussions Send Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) to Record High - Blockonomi

The stock advanced as much as 2.75%, cementing its position among this year’s top-performing chipmakers. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited, TSM The rally gained momentum after Elon Musk publicly acknowledged preliminary negotiations with TSMC concerning a potential collaboration on his ambitious Terafab venture. The project envisions a large-scale semiconductor manufacturing facility in Texas designed to meet the chip requirements of Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI. Technology reporter Tim Culpan disclosed that TSMC is examining potential strategies to assist the emerging chipmaker in operating its planned Texas production sites. Musk addressed the reports on X, stating “Just discussions, but something may come of it.” Intel’s shares experienced a contrasting fate, falling more than 2% despite the company’s April partnership announcement with Terafab. Market participants questioned the implications of potential TSMC involvement for Intel’s foundry strategy. Bloomberg revealed Thursday that TSMC is simultaneously evaluating an independent manufacturing complex in Texas. The prospective development could require investments reaching tens of billions of dollars across multiple production facilities, though negotiations remain in preliminary stages. Individual fabrication plants are anticipated to require investments of at least $20 billion each. The ultimate green light may depend on whether Congress extends the 35% advanced-manufacturing tax credit beyond its current December 2026 expiration. North American clients currently represent over 75% of TSMC’s wafer sales. Technology leaders including Nvidia and AMD rank among the company’s largest customers for cutting-edge chip production services. Deputy Co-Chief Operating Officer Cliff Hou disclosed that TSMC has approximately doubled its equipment procurement budget within the last twelve months. The expansion addresses explosive growth in AI infrastructure requirements. TSMC has pledged $265 billion toward its Arizona manufacturing footprint. Additional international initiatives are underway in Japan and Germany, with exploratory discussions happening in Singapore. Industry analyst Counterpoint Research identifies TSMC as the “central beneficiary” of artificial intelligence semiconductor expansion. The research firm highlighted second-quarter revenue climbing 34% year-over-year to $40.2 billion. TSMC’s Foundry 2.0 market position expanded to approximately 42%, compared with 38% in 2025. Counterpoint forecasts full-year 2026 revenue growth near 43%, with momentum building toward 50% expansion in the latter half. S&P Global Ratings projects hyperscaler artificial intelligence expenditures will reach $1.5 trillion by 2028. The ratings agency views TSMC as relatively insulated should that investment eventually moderate. S&P attributed TSMC’s resilience to its technological advantage and broad customer portfolio, which should preserve pricing power and margin stability. The firm anticipates profitability and cash flow will remain above 2026 benchmarks even amid softening demand scenarios. While pursuing global expansion, TSMC maintains its position that cutting-edge manufacturing processes will remain concentrated in Taiwan. Company representatives declined to address the Texas campus speculation, responding only, “We have no comment on market rumors.” TSMC’s October 15 earnings release carries significant weight on Wall Street. Consensus estimates call for EPS of $4.45, up substantially from $2.92 twelve months prior, with revenue anticipated at $45.54 billion versus $33.10 billion last year. title: Major Banks | BofA Securities: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US) maintains ties with "Musk's dynamic duo"; likelihood of sharing technology or control with Terafab remains low - 富途牛牛
content: Bank of America Securities released a research report stating that Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US) maintains strong relationships with customers associated with Elon Musk. It expects that, as Tesla (TSLA.US) and SpaceX (SPCX.US) expand their businesses, cooperation between the two sides will deepen. However, the likelihood of Taiwan Semiconductor licensing technology to Terafab or jointly operating a fab with Terafab while holding a significant equity stake is relatively low. The bank noted that on Saturday last week (the 3rd), when responding to reports about a potential manufacturing partnership between Taiwan Semiconductor and Terafab, Musk said, "It's just discussions, but there could be results." According to the bank's estimates, Tesla and SpaceX—directly (in automotive/robotics and cloud‑based AI ASICs) and indirectly (through commercial HPC chips such as GPUs and network switches)—account for roughly 2% to 3% of Taiwan Semiconductor's sales. Customer neutrality is at the heart of Taiwan Semiconductor's foundry model; its joint-venture fabs have a limited track record and mostly employ mature processes. Even for Apple (AAPL.US), which contributed roughly 21% of its revenue from 2015 to 2025 and primarily uses advanced processes, Taiwan Semiconductor does not co‑own any fabs, in order to maintain full operational control and customer neutrality. The firm further noted that, according to Terafab's application for the JETI project in Texas, the four-phase plan from 2026 to 2036 will involve approximately US$119 billion in investment, with about 60% allocated to equipment procurement. Spending from 2026 to 2028 will be heavily weighted toward facility construction, while from 2029 to 2036 annual equipment expenditures are expected to range between US$6 billion and US$8 billion. According to the firm's estimates, expanding advanced‑process capacity by 1,000 wafers per month in the U.S. would require more than US$600 million; even if the technology roadmap proceeds smoothly, Terafab could add at most around 10,000 wafers per month annually, making it difficult to achieve economies of scale. As a result, Taiwan Semiconductor will likely remain Tesla and SpaceX's primary foundry partner. The firm reiterated its "Buy" rating on Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW), assigning a 2027 projected price-to-earnings ratio of 20x (currently around 16x) and maintaining a target price of NT$3,100, believing that the stock is in the mid-cycle phase, supported by robust AI demand pipelines. title: Why Did NVDA, TSM, WBD Stocks Hit 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) and Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. (WBD) hit fresh 52-week highs on Monday as investors piled into AI infrastructure and media consolidation plays. Higher Wall Street expectations for Nvidia, potential Musk-linked chipmaking plans at TSMC and WBD’s merger progress fueled the gains. Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor stocks gained over 2%, while Warner Bros. Discovery stock ended the session 0.03% higher. Nvidia stock surged to a record high of $240.10 as BNP Paribas issued a more bullish outlook, raising its price target to $345 from $285 while maintaining an ‘Outperform’ rating. The new price target implies a 44% upside to Monday’s close. The firm sees Nvidia's combination of CUDA software, NVLink networking and Blackwell processors as a competitive advantage as demand shifts toward AI inference workloads. Nvidia is a major player in the AI boom, supported by record sales and profits. It is also expanding its reach by investing in AI companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock jumped to ‘bullish’ from ‘bearish’ territory the previous day. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing stock also reached an all-time high of $487.47 amid discussions involving Elon Musk's proposed Terafab semiconductor initiative. Under the potential arrangement, TSMC could develop and run a dedicated manufacturing operation for companies including Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. Musk confirmed that discussions are taking place but cautioned that no agreement has been finalized, writing on X, “Just discussions, but something may come of it.” Retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory the previous day. Warner Bros. Discovery stock climbed to a four-year high of $30.99 as its combination with Paramount Skydance (PSKY) moved into its final operational stage. The transition marks a major change for the entertainment company following months of deal-related uncertainty. Incoming Chairman and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz have outlined the leadership structure for the combined business. Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein will oversee film operations, while Casey Bloys will continue leading direct-to-consumer streaming. James Gunn and Peter Safran will remain in charge of DC Studios. Retail sentiment remained ‘bullish’. So far this year, NVDA, TSM and WBD stocks have gained between 7% and 60%. A booming demand for artificial intelligence has bolstered a climb in tech stocks. Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) and Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) rose more than 2% at close on Monday, while Meta Platforms Inc. (META) and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) rose more than 1%. SpaceX (SPCX), meanwhile, climbed more than 7% as its first orbital Starship flight and growing AI ambitions put the focus on the company’s long-term growth potential. Morgan Stanley Wealth Management investment chief Lisa Shalett reportedly wrote in a note that bonds have faced heightened volatility over the past six weeks, according to a CNBC report. She said that while intraday implied volatility has increased, the recent moves have yet to reach the extreme levels that preceded the 2022 equity bear market. Last week, “Bond King” Bill Gross noted in a Financial Times op-ed that markets must be prepared for the end of “what you are used to” in stock markets and higher volatility in prices for the benchmark 10-year Treasury bonds. As stocks rise to record levels and yields climb simultaneously, “my view is: don’t own bonds, with the exception of one-year Treasury bills, which are now at 4.55 percent,” he said. Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) hit their highest level since mid-June on Monday, returning CEO Elon Musk to trillionaire status as its first orbital Starship flight and growing AI ambitions put the company’s long-term growth potential in the spotlight. SPCX stock jumped nearly 8% to $171.09, lifting Musk’s fortune to about $1.04 trillion, according to Forbes’ real-time billionaires list, which includes his SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA) holdings. Shares also gained nearly 1% in after-hours trading after SpaceX proposed a 32.4-mile natural gas pipeline in Florida’s Brevard County to supply fuel for Starship launches from Cape Canaveral. “We are seeing the very beginning of investors starting to understand SpaceX,” Sequoia Capital partner Shaun Maguire said on X. He was responding to Mach33 founder and CEO Aaron Burnett, who urged investors to study SpaceX while others were still catching up. Burnett’s post discussed Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas’ observation that few clients appeared to own the stock. In an excerpt shared by Tesla investor and influencer Sawyer Merritt, Jonas recalled asking 40 clients whether anyone owned SPCX shares. “Not a single hand went up,” he said. Jonas argued that assessing SpaceX solely through telecommunications, aerospace and defense, or AI misses the connections between its businesses. “Valuing SPCX is more of an ‘and’ problem than an ‘or’ problem,” he said. “The unusual dimensionality that makes it challenging to value the stock, in and of itself, gives the stock its value.” Burnett questioned why the “loudest” voices on asset pricing often had done the “least work” to understand underlying value, while acknowledging a place for both valuation shortcuts and technical research. “SpaceX is among the most difficult technology suites in the world to ‘intuit’ and getting more complex not less,” he said. “The complexity is equally a challenge and opportunity, depends on your perspective.” Wells Fargo said SpaceX is redeploying engineers from its launch and connectivity divisions to orbital data center work, prioritizing AI satellites ahead of a demonstration launch targeted for the second quarter of 2027. Scaled deployment would follow once Starship supports a faster launch cadence. Last week highlighted the breadth of its operations: SpaceX launched a NASA crew to the International Space Station, sent Google AI chips into orbit on a separate flight and deployed next-generation Starlink satellites aboard Starship. Musk also said SpaceXAI would become SpaceXSI, embracing U.S. President Donald Trump’s superintelligence branding. ARK Investment Management analysts Tasha Keeney and Daniel Maguire said Starship is “reshaping the industry once again,” estimating that Flight 14’s 26 Starlink V3 satellites could support nearly $560 million in annualized revenue. The estimate applies SpaceX’s reported second-quarter revenue run-rate to the added downlink capacity. A fully loaded Starship could deliver about 20 times the bandwidth of a Falcon 9 launch carrying V2 Minis, ARK said. The bigger opportunity rests on full reusability, which ARK estimates could cut launch costs to $100 per kilogram or less at scale and make orbital data centers economically feasible. Frontier-model AI could represent more than 90% of SpaceX’s stated $28.5 trillion addressable market, the firm said. “A successful upper-stage catch would put full reusability—and a new era of launch economics—within reach,” ARK said. Morgan Stanley said that a potential catch could be “the biggest positive catalyst since the IPO.” Meanwhile, Wells Fargo offered a later timeline, calling a booster catch a reasonable target but a ship catch “likely a late ’27 / early ’28 story.” Morgan Stanley’s $300 target implies about 75% upside from Monday’s close. Wells Fargo rates shares ‘overweight’ with a $212 target, implying about 24% upside. One user said, “$SPCX $300 bull target my Morgan Stanley. Will probably get there in the next 2 years. Will be a bumpy ride. I can’t wrap my mind around a company that would be worth more than Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon combined haha. If it ever reaches $1000 a share. It would be the worlds richest company. Hard to even fathom that” Another bullish user said, “$SPCX It's not too late to hop on the boat. This is one of those once-in-a-generation opportunity, kinda like Tesla in the early days.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. (NVAX) jumped 20% on Monday, clocking its best session since January, as a rival’s strong trial result lifted vaccine stocks amid speculation about a plague outbreak in Russia. Moderna shares rose about 7%, a move also tied to its pending addition to the Nasdaq-100, while BioNTech edged 1% higher after Vaxcyte announced positive trial results for its pneumonia vaccine. Separately, reports of a suspected plague outbreak in Russia also triggered sectorwide optimism. Vaxcyte said earlier on Monday that its experimental pneumonia vaccine, VAX-31, met the main goals of a late-stage study in adults 50 and older. The shot is designed to cover 31 strains of the bacteria that cause pneumococcal disease, which can lead to pneumonia, meningitis and bloodstream infections. In the study, immune responses were at least comparable to Pfizer’s Prevnar 20 and Merck’s Capvaxive on the strains those vaccines already cover, and stronger on three strains unique to VAX-31. Vaxcyte said the safety profile was consistent across the age groups tested. Vaxcyte shares rose 31% in regular trading and revived interest in vaccine makers. Novavax’s own story is about partnerships. In late August, the company said partners Sanofi and Takeda had won approval for an updated version of its protein-based COVID-19 vaccine, Nuvaxovid, in the United States, the European Union and Japan ahead of the 2026–2027 season. In the U.S., the shot is cleared for people 65 and older and for those 12 to 64 with a condition that raises the risk of severe illness. Sanofi holds the commercial rights in most markets and is carrying the vaccine into the fall season in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany and Canada. Novavax no longer sells it itself. It collects royalties on partner sales and is still due a $75 million manufacturing technology-transfer payment, which it has said it expects in the fourth quarter. Over the weekend, reports circulated that a Russian lab worker has died from a possible case of pneumonic plague while working at the Research Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia. The reports are unconfirmed. According to a report from Axios, President Trump said on Monday that the U.S. will help Russia in case of a pneumonic plague outbreak. Axios also reported that the White House is monitoring the outbreak. Novavax, however, has no plague vaccine. Federal energy officials announced a conditional $4.2 billion loan commitment Monday to modernize and boost power production across nuclear generation facilities in Pennsylvania and Ohio, targeting rising regional electricity costs and surging energy demand. The funding, extended by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing to Texas-based utility operator Vistra (VST), aims to expand generation capacity across existing facilities without necessitating new power transmission infrastructure. According to department officials, the initiative supports executive measures to bolster domestic nuclear infrastructure and restore American energy output. The planned upgrades focus on Vistra’s Beaver Valley plant in Pennsylvania, along with the Davis-Besse and Perry facilities in Ohio. By executing thermodynamic and hardware uprates, the project will add 433 megawatts of power capacity while maintaining nearly 4 gigawatts of steady baseload electricity—enough to supply power to more than 3 million households. Earlier in January this year, Meta Platforms (META) struck 20-year agreements to buy power from Vistra’s Perry and Davis-Besse plants in Ohio and Beaver Valley plant in Pennsylvania. Beyond expanding immediate output, the modernization strategy will help extend operational life cycles at the three Midwestern plants by up to 20 years beyond their current licensing terms. The conditional loan arrangement also leaves open an option to fund future uprates at Vistra’s Comanche Peak facility in Texas. Construction, engineering, and specialized maintenance during scheduled outage periods are projected to support about 3,000 temporary jobs while protecting thousands of permanent operational positions at the facilities. By boosting generation within established facility footprints, the funding addresses growing power consumption across the 13-state PJM Interconnection grid, which serves major industrial and residential centers throughout the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions. Final disbursement of the $4.2 billion loan remains contingent on Vistra meeting mandatory environmental, legal, technical, and financial criteria required by federal regulators. title: Why Is TSM Stock Rising Premarket? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. rose 0.6% in early premarket trading on Monday after the contract chipmaker’s monthly sales update showed continued robust demand for AI and chips. Revenue in July rose 45% to NT$467.58 billion ($14.5 billion). Analysts on average are estimating a 46.8% increase in sales for the current quarter, Q3. The latest performance shows steady demand for advanced chips, which power data centers and other systems that power AI applications, smartphones and automobiles. TSMC makes cutting-edge semiconductors for the likes of Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. The biggest buyers of those chips – including cloud companies Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft – have set aside about $800 billion for AI-related investments this year. Last month, TSMC raised its spending and revenue projections for the year, reflecting confidence in demand for chips powering AI development. TSMC now expects its capital expenditure to reach a record level of $60 billion to $64 billion in 2026 and forecasts its full-year sales to grow slightly above 40% in U.S. dollar terms. Separately, Sony Group and TSMC announced a plan to spend around ‌1 trillion yen ($6.32 billion) to jointly ‌make next-generation microchips used in image sensors, the Nikkei ​business daily said on Monday. A joint venture owned about 60% by Sony and 40% by TSMC will start commercial production as early ‌as 2029 in ⁠southern Japan's Kumamoto prefecture, the paper said. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for TSMC remained ‘bearish,’ unchanged from the previous day, with several users posting about the monthly update. title: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) Breaks to $485.80, a New 52-Week High - 24/7 Wall St.
content: As seen on the 24/7 Wall St. homepage on October 5, 2026. Taiwan Semiconductor cleared its June 30 peak by 1.99% with a new 52-week high at $485.80, a fresh record for a $2.5 trillion foundry that anchors the entire AI chip supply chain. The next test is whether it holds above the old ceiling. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing cleared its previous 52-week peak, set on June 30, by nearly 2% to reach $485.80. That prior ceiling had stood for months, so breaking cleanly above it carries technical weight beyond the round-number milestone. The company sits at the center of the AI chip supply chain as the world's dominant contract chipmaker, manufacturing the advanced processors that power everything from data-center GPUs to consumer devices. A fresh record for a company of this scale reflects sustained conviction that demand for leading-edge semiconductor fabrication is not slowing. The advance has been a persistent climb rather than a single-day spike. That kind of steady, broad advance tends to signal durable institutional participation. The immediate question for investors is whether the stock can hold above its former high at the June 30 level. A breakout that consolidates above a prior peak is typically viewed as more durable than one that retreats back below it, making the next several sessions important for gauging how lasting this move will be. Nearly two years in Eric Bleeker's AI Portfolio, and the foundry that makes almost every leading AI chip has more than doubled: $1,000 at the October 2024 call is worth about $2,326 today. Anyone waiting for the geopolitical discount to close first has paid for the wait. Two years in Eric Bleeker's AI Portfolio turned $10,000 into roughly $26,400 on the world's most indispensable chipmaker. The position cleared the double mark long ago and keeps extending as AI foundry demand compounds. Two years in Eric Bleeker's AI Portfolio, and Taiwan Semiconductor has turned a $10,000 stake into roughly $26,420. The foundry that makes nearly every leading AI chip is still the cleanest way to own the buildout. The sale was the biggest leg of the three, and the filing landed 41 days later, so the repositioning only becomes public now. (TSLA) heads into next week's second-quarter (Q2) earnings with growing pressure from its retail investor base, as Robotaxi delays, missed milestones, and the Optimus production ramp dominate shareholder questions. TSLA stock is down 3% so far this week, with shares also down 0.3% in premarket trading on Thursday. Robotaxi is by far the dominant theme among the highest-ranked retail questions. The EV giant is expected to report its Q2 results on July 22. One of the most-upvoted submissions asks why Tesla has repeatedly missed its own autonomy targets: "Tesla has missed short term guidance on robotaxi 3 earnings reports in a row... What is keeping Tesla back from accomplishing these short term goals that they've set for themselves?" Another asks: "Why has growth of robotaxi vehicles stalled? When will we see Cybercab start customer rides?" Investors are also demanding concrete operating metrics, including fleet size, paid rides, intervention rates, cost per mile and revenue contribution, instead of broader progress updates. Others want revised rollout milestones after earlier targets were missed. Musk said in 2019 that Tesla could have one million Robotaxis on the road by the end of 2020, a target that never materialized as Full Self-Driving (FSD) remained a supervised system. Tesla reset expectations during its October 2024 Cybercab unveiling, targeting unsupervised Robotaxi operations in Texas and California in 2025 and volume production of Cybercabs in 2026. The company launched a limited paid Robotaxi service in Austin in June 2025 before beginning production of Cybercab earlier this year, though Musk cautioned that the initial production ramp would be "agonizingly slow." Optimus was the second most-discussed topic, with shareholders seeking updates on Gen 3 production, factory deployment and commercial rollout. The highest-ranked Optimus question asks about the Gen 3 production ramp, initial factory deployment and external sales timeline for 2027. Others ask how many Optimus robots are currently working inside Tesla factories, what tasks they perform and what manufacturing bottlenecks still stand in the way of mass production. The questions mirror Robotaxi concerns. Tesla first targeted limited Optimus production in 2023 before shifting toward low-rate production and internal factory deployment through 2026. Musk has said that the ramp for Optimus is also "agonizingly slow," arguing that nearly every component is new. Koyfin estimates call for Q2 revenue of $26.29 billion, up 17% from a year ago. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) is expected to rise 31% to $0.54. Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $417 from $415 and maintained an 'Equal Weight' rating, implying a 6% upside from current levels. The firm expects a solid quarter but continues to view Robotaxi and Optimus as the primary long-term value drivers. Barclays lifted its target to $370 and reiterated an 'Equal Weight' rating, implying a 6% downside, while Wells Fargo raised its target to $130 and maintained an 'Underweight' rating, implying a 67% downside. Jefferies raised its target to $400 from $375 while maintaining a 'Hold' rating, implying a 1% upside. The firm cited Tesla's delivery beat but warned that implied Cybercab production still points to further delays in the Robotaxi ramp. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for TSLA slipped to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 66% jump in 24-hour message volume. One user said, “$TSLA clearly has been some strength since it’s been holding this level. With one option remaining for Friday leading into earnings week, I do expect a nice bounce tomorrow.” Another user said, “$TSLA it feels like this wants to flush before next weeks earnings then skyrocket afterwards.” So far this year, Tesla's stock has lagged its "Magnificent Seven" peers, making it the group's second-worst performer, down 12%. (UBER) have entered into a partnership to deliver everything from the latest game releases to consoles and accessories for on-demand or scheduled delivery across the U.S. The partnership marks another step in Uber Eats' push beyond restaurant deliveries as the platform continues adding retailers across categories such as groceries, electronics, beauty, and home improvement. For GameStop, the move offers another avenue to reach customers seeking faster access to gaming products without visiting a store. GameStop shares were up nearly 0.1% in Wednesday’s pre-market trade, while Uber shares were up about 1%. Customers can now order a wide range of products from participating GameStop stores through the Uber Eats app, including video games, gaming consoles, controllers, accessories, collectibles, and other consumer electronics. Orders can be placed for either on-demand or scheduled delivery, giving shoppers another way to purchase gaming products without visiting a physical store. Uber said the partnership is designed to make it easier for customers to get gaming essentials when they need them, whether it's replacing a controller before a game night, buying a newly released title on launch day, or picking up a last-minute gift. “Adding GameStop to Uber Eats strengthens our growing gaming and electronics selection, giving customers access to another trusted retailer they can shop with the speed and convenience they know from Uber,” said Uber’s Head of Grocery and Retail in North America, Hashim Amin. The addition also expands Uber Eats' growing selection of non-food retail offerings. To place an order, customers can browse the Retail or Electronics category in the Uber Eats app, search for GameStop, select their items, and choose a delivery time. Once the order is placed, customers can then track it in real time, similar to restaurant deliveries. GameStop is the latest retailer to join Uber Eats as the company continues expanding beyond restaurant deliveries. The platform recently added merchants across categories including beauty, office supplies, sporting goods, pet supplies, and consumer electronics as it seeks to become a broader marketplace for everyday shopping. Last month, Uber announced partnerships with retailers including Kiehl's, FedEx Office, Blick Art Materials, Academy Sports + Outdoors, and Choice Pet, adding thousands of additional storefronts to its marketplace. The company said the expansion builds on a retail network that already includes brands such as Sephora, The Home Depot, and Best Buy. Uber has said consumers are increasingly using the app for more than meals, prompting it to invest in new retail categories and on-demand delivery for a wider range of products. The addition of GameStop further expands its electronics and gaming offerings, giving customers another option for same-day delivery of consoles, games, and accessories. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) is the IBD Stock Of The Day as the world's top contract chipmaker, better known as TSMC, is in talks to take a role in Elon Musk's planned Terafab chip factory. TSM stock surged on the news. The surge on Monday sent TSM stock past a buy point of 479 in a cup base. In intraday trading, it notched a record high of 487.44. On the stock market today, TSM rose 2.8% to close at 485.80. On Sept. 8, IBD analysis pointed to the first of several early-entry buy points for TSM stock at 436.04. It cleared another early entry on Sept. 21 as it rebounded strongly off its 50-day moving average line and cleared short-term highs. TSMC's relative strength line hit new highs on Monday. That provides a bullish corroboration of the breakout.  At the same time, the stock is now more than 10% above its 50-day line. That means — despite the breakout — it could also be due for some consolidation.  This is particularly true with earnings due Oct. 15. On Saturday, in a post on his social-media site X, Musk confirmed that discussions with TSMC were underway, saying, "Just discussions, but something may come of it." He also responded "true" to another post that said Terafab would be "absurdly massive" and anything TSMC contributes would be "supplemental." News reports further supported TSMC's talks with Musk about participating in Terafab. Tim Culpan's Culpium newsletter on Friday reported that TSMC would build and operate a facility exclusively serving Tesla (TSLA), Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX), and xAI. The likeliest structure for the deal would have TSMC owning and operating the fab with SpaceX investing, committing to volume, or both, Culpium said. Wedbush Securities analyst Matt Bryson on Monday reiterated his outperform rating on TSM stock following the news reports. However, the reports were negative news for Intel (INTC), which joined the Terafab project in April. On Monday, Intel stock dropped 2.6% to close at 116.19. A Terafab deal with TSMC "would make total sense as they are recognized as the best in the world at large-scale leading-edge node semi manufacturing," Mizuho Securities trading-desk analyst Jordan Klein said in a client note. "I think news last week that TSM is exploring a new U.S. manufacturing hub in Texas would be part of this project with Musk being the anchor customer." Further, the Terafab project likely would be shared or split between TSMC and Intel, he said. The next potential catalyst for TSM stock could be the company's September monthly sales report, due on Thursday. title: New Record in TSM Stock, Eyeing $500 as TSMC Explores Role in Musk TeraFab - FXLeaders
content: TSM stock has climbed to fresh record highs above $480 as strong NVIDIA results reinforce semiconductor demand and potential TSMC involvement in Elon Musk’s TeraFab adds another growth catalyst. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing shares have extended their rally above $480, surpassing the previous record from June and moving toward the psychologically important $500 level. The latest momentum comes as investors assess the potential for TSMC to participate in Elon Musk’s $16.8 billion TeraFab project in Texas. Musk has confirmed that discussions with TSMC are underway, although he indicated that negotiations remain at an early stage. Intel was previously identified as a manufacturing partner after joining the project in April, with its 14A process technology selected for the proposed facility. However, reports that TSMC is exploring a role could create an additional opportunity for the world’s largest advanced-chip foundry. The potential partnership follows reports that TSMC is considering expanding its manufacturing presence in Texas after developing its Arizona operations. Reports have suggested TSMC could eventually establish multiple advanced fabs in Texas. One possibility would involve TSMC owning and operating a new facility while SpaceX participates through equity investment or guaranteed purchase agreements. The TeraFab concept was initially proposed by Musk in 2025 after he argued that existing semiconductor supply would not be sufficient for Tesla’s long-term requirements. In March 2026, Musk announced plans for a semiconductor facility in Austin, Texas, positioned near Tesla’s headquarters and intended as a joint venture between Tesla and SpaceX. Intel subsequently joined the project, but the potential involvement of TSMC could broaden the manufacturing strategy. NVIDIA’s latest results provide another major catalyst for TSM stock. NVIDIA operates a fabless model, designing its processors while relying on external manufacturers such as TSMC for production. TSMC manufactures the majority of NVIDIA’s most advanced chips, meaning continued growth in GPU demand directly supports demand for TSMC’s leading-edge manufacturing capacity. Strong NVIDIA revenue and expectations for continued infrastructure spending therefore reinforce the broader semiconductor cycle. Unlike NVIDIA, which must justify extremely high growth expectations, TSMC can benefit from demand generated by multiple customers across the semiconductor industry. TSM stock was already showing strong momentum before NVIDIA released its results, and the move above $487 suggests investors are increasingly positioning for continued growth in advanced semiconductor demand. The company’s manufacturing leadership gives it a central role in the production of high-end chips used by major technology companies. The same spending boom supporting TSM stock also creates longer-term risks. Semiconductor companies are committing enormous amounts of capital to computing infrastructure, advanced processors and new manufacturing facilities. For TSMC, this creates opportunities for higher revenue and utilization, but expectations are becoming increasingly elevated. If NVIDIA’s growth slows or customers reduce infrastructure spending, semiconductor orders could eventually weaken. There is also a risk that aggressive investment creates excess capacity if supply expands faster than underlying demand. For now, buyers remain firmly in control as TSM stock trades above $480 and approaches the $500 psychological level. A sustained breakout above $500 could reinforce the broader uptrend, while failure to hold the new record zone could trigger profit-taking. With potential TeraFab involvement and strong NVIDIA-driven demand supporting the story, TSMC remains positioned to benefit from the semiconductor investment cycle. However, the increasingly aggressive spending environment means investors will need to watch both demand growth and capacity expansion closely.

title: Did Halloween Already Happen in Colorado? - Retro 102.5
content: October is less than a week in, and many are excited about getting ready for Halloween. Decorations are going up in yards across the state, on balconies, and many people are getting ready for the month ahead. Halloween movies are on television, kids are wearing their costumes around the house, and many adults have begun testing the candy to make sure it is good this year. While most would assume Halloween season is ramping up, you would have a hard time guessing that by walking into certain stores. Did Halloween already take place in Colorado, and residents forgot to be told it happened already? Have you been into Costco recently? If the answer is yes, what holiday mood did the store put you in? The answer likely isn't Halloween, and during October shouldn't it be? This is the time of year when Halloween is the focal point, but as many stores have been doing through the years, they no longer respect the current season and instead are focusing on the next holiday and trying to beat their competitors to getting out their decor. Costco currently has rows of Christmas decorations, advent calendars, wrapping paper, and great gift ideas. While some have begun their holiday shopping, should Halloween be swept under the rug this soon, when the holiday is still weeks away from happening? Far too many stores are moving from one holiday to another so soon that they neglect the one that is currently in season. Not everyone is ready to move on when trunk-or-treats have not started yet, pumpkin patches only recently opened, and many do not have their costumes yet or even know what they are going to be this year. While it makes sense from a business perspective to be the first to get out holiday decorations, is now the right time to go all in on Christmas? There is nothing wrong with having a mix of Christmas and Halloween. But to fully eliminate Halloween and have more Christmas seems absurd. When do you think is the right time to go all in on Christmas? Is it the week of Halloween when most things are bought? Is it the day after Halloween? Or are you traditional and believe it should be the week of or day after Thanksgiving?

title: 3 No-Brainer Stocks to Buy If Data Center Expenditures Hit $3 Trillion by 2030 - The Globe and Mail
content: Nvidia holds the largest market share in the AI compute market. Micron and Taiwan Semiconductor are critical suppliers to Nvidia and its peers. It's no secret that the artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscalers are dumping billions of dollars into data centers to provide enough computing power to train their AI models along with running existing workloads. There's not enough computing capacity to go around, and it will be several years before there is enough to meet the demand of an AI-first economy. Nvidia(NASDAQ: NVDA) believes that AI spending will grow to $3 trillion to $4 trillion annually by 2030, which indicates a massive growth runway. If that projection pans out, there are a handful of stocks that are no-brainer buys -- namely, Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor(NYSE: TSM), and Micron(NASDAQ: MU). All three of these stocks are set to cash in big time if data center capital expenditures hit that level, and each looks like a solid investment to make right now. Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Nvidia is clearly the market leader in terms of AI computing units. While the competition is getting stiffer, Nvidia holds a massive market share lead that cannot be topped. During the second quarter, it generated $96 billion in revenue, with the bulk of that coming from data center products. Next quarter, that figure is expected to rise to $108 billion. Nvidia is far from done growing too. During its last earnings call, it told investors that it expects 70% revenue growth during 2027. With the AI build-out expected to intensify through 2030, there's a monster runway for Nvidia to grow into. However, the market doesn't respect this projection. Nvidia trades for an incredibly cheap price tag of less than 15 times next year's earnings. If Nvidia hits all analyst projections, and trades for 30 times earnings at the end of next year (an entirely reasonable valuation for a company growing that fast), the stock would be primed to double. That makes it a smart buy now, and I think investors will be well rewarded for buying Nvidia shares today. Nvidia doesn't make any of the components that go into its chips; it just designs them. That's where Taiwan Semiconductor and Micron come in. Both of these companies are chip foundries, but they focus on different types of chips. Taiwan Semiconductor produces logic chips, while Micron makes memory chips. Each of these companies is vital to the function of computing chips like Nvidia, but also for its competitors. There aren't a lot of options in the chip foundry world, so most companies end up working with these two. That makes them fairly neutral investments in the AI race, and if you believe that Nvidia is primed to lose market share, then these two hedge that bet. Micron and Taiwan Semiconductor may not have the upside that Nvidia or its peers have. Still, they are also pretty much guaranteed to continue rising if AI data center capital expenditures continue to rise. There are several projections, including Nvidia's, that say this, which makes it a pretty solid investment thesis. Right now, Micron is producing stronger growth than Taiwan Semiconductor. That's because the memory chip space is in a serious supply crunch, and chip prices are skyrocketing as a result. This won't last forever, but as of now, Micron looks to have more upside for this reason. Still, Taiwan Semiconductor is in a great spot, as it holds a dominant 72.5% revenue share in the chip foundry space as of Q2 2026. Both companies are great investments and make for a great diversification bet alongside Nvidia. All three of these stocks are slated to cash in if the AI race ramps up through 2030. I'm a firm believer that that will happen, making these three stocks excellent buys now.
